root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `memchr()` relocates `p`, `memsearch_swar()` must re-evaluate the remaining haystack span from `p` to `e` and require `(e - p) >= m` before permitting the fallback `memcmp()`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable fallback guard still tests stale `len < m` from before `memchr()` moved `p`. On the crashing path `p` relocates to `ys + 26`, leaving only `e - p == 2` bytes, but the sink still executes. The fixed version restores the missing post-`memchr` span check and guards the sink on the stock PoC.

nodes.state: The same candidate offset returned by `memchr()` reaches the fallback `memcmp()` call even though fewer than `m` bytes remain from `p` to `e`.

When the sink-side `memcmp(p+1, xs+1, m-1)` executes on the vulnerable witness, the remaining haystack span `e - p` is smaller than the full needle length `m`, so the compare begins from a near-end candidate that cannot safely satisfy the request.

edges.relation: The relocated candidate position chosen by `memchr()` at the stale guard site is the same source-level candidate position immediately consumed by the following fallback `memcmp()` call.
